title: Raymond Brown and hearing bands from the street
summary: Raymond Brown, his father-in-law, a good trombonist; hearing dance bands at the clubs from the street.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah. I was going to ask about your father-in-law's name is, what was your first name?
And, uh, I know Harold said he was a wonderful trombonist. Well, Harold played with him.
Yeah, he was a good trombonist. Harold played with him. I never did play with him. You never did?
No. He was on the road when I was at the dance floor. Yeah.

Can you remember any of the other early, the very earliest recollections that you have of any music when you were a boy? Any bands, even if you were too small to go into a place, did you hear any dances or the bands from outside? Of course you said you heard all the wagons at all.
Well, yeah, we could, and we could hear them from around the Duet Club or the Tulane Club. We'd stand on the outside and they said I'd play then with the dancers.
Remember who played there most of them?
No, I didn't know the fellas during them times, but some of them would still live now, but just like Pazio, Alfred Williams, and all them, they was playing during that time.
